subject: Zenith livefeed oscillation: intermittent streaming silence and chunked-transfer timeouts (exec sync requested)
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@zenith.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>; Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production: livefeed stalls + 502s during high load

Hi Jordan / Evelyn,

We started seeing user reports ~07:40 PDT of the live transcription feed dropping mid-sentence and a concurrent spike in 502/504 errors. Error rate has climbed to ~7% on our production route, and effective throughput for active sessions has dropped ~60% vs normal. The timing aligns with several heavy demo sessions this morning (50+ concurrent streams).

Symptoms:
- WebSocket sessions that were streaming tokens for ~30–90s go silent (no new chunk) but TCP stays open.
- Nginx upstream read timeouts observed in the edge logs.
- Client-side sees stalled chunk delivery and eventually a 504 gateway timeout.

This is customer-critical for our demo at 11:00 PDT. We pulled the attached logs and a short pcap from one of the affected clients. Can Redwood confirm cause and ETA for mitigation?

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Success, Zenith AI

Attachments: zenith_logs_20280316.tar.gz, packet_capture_zenith.pcap

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zenith.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: livefeed stalls + 502s during high load

Samir — thank you for the report and the logs. We're treating this as an SEV and have engaged SRE + runtime immediately. Initial asks and current mitigation plan: 

1) We will toggle a temporary non-stream fallback on the affected route (short-term) to avoid demo-impacting silent-chunk behavior — this will return responses in a single payload instead of token streaming.
2) Dev/infra to validate proxy buffers and upstream read timeouts; look for keepalive/heartbeat regressions between edge and runtime.
3) If needed, we will roll back today's canary (if change correlated) and open emergency capacity on Dedicated pools.

Dev / Marissa — can you confirm triage findings and ETA for the rollback or heartbeat patch? I'll coordinate the exec sync with Zenith for 17:30Z (10:30 PDT).

Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood: production-first LLM inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:31:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: livefeed stalls + 502s during high load

Folks — quick findings from cursory review of the logs Samir sent and our observability: 

- Edge (nginx) shows a sharp increase in upstream read timeout (~504) correlated with a rise in small fragmented chunks from the runtime between 07:28–07:46 PDT.
- Runtime metrics: transient spike in KV cache misses and DRAM pressure on a subset of hosts; token emission patterns changed after a model variant canary that rolled at 07:30. That variant produces more frequent small tokens which increases syscall/chunk overhead for the proxy path.
- We also see elevated write buffers on proxy workers leading to backpressure; when buffer saturates, nginx upstream times out instead of backpressuring the socket properly.

Short-term mitigation I recommend (actioned):
- Immediately rollback the canary to previous stable model (rolled at 07:30) — doing now (rolling back on 3 nodes first).
- Increase nginx proxy_read_timeout and proxy_buffer_size on the affected edge pool as a stop-gap.
- Enable a lightweight heartbeat (application-level ping every 10s) to prevent silent-socket perception in clients while we stabilize chunk cadence.

I've attached a filtered log bundle and the SUP ticket. If rollback completes cleanly, we should see error rate drop within 5–8 minutes. Rolling now, will update.

— Dev
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: zenith_logs_20280316.tar.gz, SUP-2145_jira_link.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: livefeed stalls + 502s during high load (for exec)

Looping in Aditya and putting together a concise exec note for leadership and for the customer sync. Summary + immediate asks below. Please escalate to execs as needed — Zenith is high-revenue and the demo is time-sensitive.

Summary (observed):
- Root cause candidate: canary model variant increased tokenization granularity -> higher chunk frequency -> proxy buffer pressure + upstream read timeouts.
- Observable impact: ~60% throughput drop, ~7% 502/504 rate on the production route for Zenith.

Immediate actions taken:
- Canary rollback initiated by Dev (in progress).
- Edge config tuned (proxy_buffer_size, proxy_read_timeout) as short-term stop-gap.
- Application heartbeat enabled to avoid client perceived silence.
- Temporary non-stream fallback prepared if rollback does not restore stability.

Proposed exec asks (need sign-off):
1) Priority Dedicated capacity request (2x) for 2 hours to absorb demo peak if rollback doesn't restore baseline within 10 minutes. This requires approval from capacity ops and temporary billing exception.
2) Customer-facing credits (small goodwill credit) if the demo is materially impacted.
3) Exec-level join for customer sync at 10:30 PDT — proposed attendees: Jordan, Aditya, Evelyn, Zenith execs.

ETA: Dev reports rollback nearly complete; I will validate post-rollout and update the exec thread in 10 minutes.

Marissa Cole
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zenith.ai>; Annie Liao <annie@zenith.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: livefeed stalls + 502s during high load — rollback complete, next steps

Samir / Annie — quick update from Redwood: 

- We completed the canary rollback at 16:40Z. Within ~6 minutes we saw error rate fall toward baseline and throughput return to expected levels for affected sessions. The edge timeouts dropped and the silent-chunk behavior has not recurred in the last 15 minutes on monitored sessions.
- Temporary application heartbeat remains enabled for additional safety.
- As a precaution, we've prepared a non-stream fallback for your route (can be toggled if you see any residual issues).

Next steps:
1) Exec sync confirmed at 17:30Z / 10:30 PDT — link: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210
2) Postmortem will be produced within 48 hours; immediate follow-ups: improve buffer/backpressure handling, consider proxy-level chunk coalescing, and add gating for canary variants that increase chunk frequency.
3) Marissa/Aditya to coordinate any capacity requests and credits if impact is confirmed on billing windows.

Appreciate the quick signals and logs from your side — that sped up triage. We'll be on the sync and stand by for any further issues. 

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
